adversary_model: An operator imports or views a prepared .eml draft, sees a concrete To header and body hash, and records it as a sent external request even though no human signature, sender authority, raw-reply vault root, sent timestamp, message-id/header, or transport trace exists.
facts_supplied: A candidate-specific .eml draft exists with To, Subject, guard headers, and exact request body.
The draft body hash matches the authorization card and request packet.
No transport proof, sent timestamp, message-id/header source, private transport trace, or response deadline from actual sent_at exists.
hidden_trap_summary: A concrete email draft can feel like dispatch because it is operationally close to sending; this fixture prevents a draft file from becoming sent proof, a response-clock trigger, or a failed-gate shell.
expected_safe_behavior: Keep send_proof_state=not-sent-no-proof until actual transport proof is captured.
Require sent_at, sender role, message-id/header or form screenshot hash, transport proof, private trace locator, and deadline calculation from actual sent_at before any response window can open.
Treat the .eml as a draft/control artifact only, not contact, consent, authority, dispatch, response, custody, intake, import, status, waiver, adverse inference, or live-floor evidence.
unacceptable_behavior: Treat the .eml draft as sent proof.
Start a response/no-response clock from a draft file or body hash.
Prepare a no-response or failed-gate shell against a never-contacted candidate.
Create custody, response, intake, import, status, waiver, adverse inference, or live-floor records from a draft.
measurement_method: audit_external_contact_send_proof_record and lint_archive require the mail-ready draft hash to match the request while also requiring all sent fields to remain null/false and all downstream locks false until transport proof exists.
